summary.verdict: YES (real but PATHOGEN-SPECIFIC) — adding the FOLD1-validated StructuralHomologyProvider to the REAL substrate improves isolated-pathogen target recovery: pooled recovery@k rises 30 -> 41 (+11), and 16 of the 65 SEQUENCE-BLIND targets are lifted into the top-k shortlist — through the substrate's real tiered composition, by plugging in ONE new provider without touching the core (the living-net design). **HONEST BOUNDS (falsify-first on our own positive): (1) the recovery@k gain is CONCENTRATED IN P. FALCIPARUM (15->26); the other 3 pathogens are +0 on recovery@k and gain only 1-2 shortlist rescues — so this is a pathogen-specific rescue, not a uniform lift. (2) The engine's abstentions drop to ~0 mainly because Foldseek finds SOME structural hit for nearly every protein (structure is rarely blind), which also lowers abstention for non-targets — so the abstention drop is largely MECHANICAL and is NOT itself a quality gain; recovery@k is the honest metric.** Still, it concretely expands the vision's reach into the phylogenetically-isolated class that SUBSTRATE4 fully abstained on, and structure alone is a single RANK signal so these never reach the engine's high-confidence tier (needs 2 signals). SCOPE: ranking-quality on real homology scores; hypotheses w/ provenance, not validated targets; AlphaFold predicted structures; not wet-lab.
